clue.text: Folk that stray — not we — could be on everybody's lips

indicators.note: things that stray wander out of their places, so the letters of the surrounding words are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A remark that wayward people, unlike ourselves, are the subject of everyone's gossip.
explanation.walkthrough: The dashes make 'not we' look like an aside excluding the speakers, but NOT and WE join FOLK and THAT as fodder for 'stray'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something widely gossiped about is on everybody's lips, an idiom for the subject of general conversation.

clue.text: Feeler misses a point thanks to student of pregnancy

indicators.note: the feeler goes without one of its letters, here a single compass point

parts.note: an antenna is an insect's feeler
N, north, is a point of the compass
TA is informal British for thank you
L for learner, as on a learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: An insect loses a feeler and credits a pregnancy researcher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'misses' takes one N out of ANTENNA, leaving ANTENA.
explanation.definitionFit: Antenatal describes the period before birth, so it is an adjective meaning relating to pregnancy.

clue.text: 12's cat sees king beheading Russian novelist

parts.note: K is the chess and card abbreviation for king

indicators.note: cutting off the head removes the novelist's first letter

parts.note: Maxim Gorky was a Russian writer

explanation.surface: A comic's cat watches a king decapitate a Russian author.
explanation.walkthrough: 12 is DANDY, the British children's comic; Korky the Cat was its long-running cover star. 'beheading' takes the G off GORKY.
explanation.definitionFit: Korky the Cat was the famous feline strip character on the front of the Dandy comic.

clue.text: Too much liquid left in what one eats?

indicators.note: the letter for left is placed inside the word for what one eats

parts.note: food is what one eats

explanation.surface: A diner wonders whether leftover gravy swamping the plate is too much.
explanation.definitionFit: A flood is an overflowing excess of water, more liquid than can be contained.

clue.text: Carrier holds aptly named football manager having strained his voice?

indicators.note: the carrier contains the manager's name within it

parts.note: a hod is a builder's trough for carrying bricks
Arsene Wenger managed Arsenal, so his first name fits his club

explanation.surface: A football manager, aptly named for his club, has shouted himself hoarse on the touchline.
explanation.walkthrough: Arsene Wenger was Arsenal's manager for over twenty years, hence 'aptly named'.
explanation.definitionFit: Hoarsened means made rough or husky, as a voice becomes after straining it by shouting.

clue.text: Nasty rotten hue, as far as that goes

indicators.note: something nasty is in a bad state, signalling that the letters are to be messed up

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone complains about an unpleasant decaying colour, with a qualifying shrug.
explanation.definitionFit: Thereunto is an archaic adverb meaning to that point or thing, hence as far as that goes.

clue.text: Listener to twig the old religion?

indicators.note: a listener hears the word rather than reading it, so we want a word that sounds like it

parts.note: wicker is woven from pliant twigs

explanation.surface: A question about tuning in to a branch of the ancient faith.
explanation.walkthrough: In non-rhotic British speech WICKER and WICCA sound the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Wicca is modern witchcraft, presented by its followers as a revival of pre-Christian pagan religion.

clue.text: From bottom of France to remote Surrey town's dues to 12

parts.note: fond is the French word for bottom
far means remote
Ewell is a town in Surrey, England; the 's gives S

explanation.surface: A journey from the south of France to a distant English town.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'bottom of France' as the south; it is the French word for bottom. The Dandy comic ended its print run in 2012, so goodbyes were owed to it.
explanation.definitionFit: Affectionate goodbyes were what the Dandy was owed as it ceased printing, so they are its dues.

clue.text: Test for doctor at first on a line

parts.note: an intern is a junior hospital doctor
I, the Roman numeral one, stands for first

explanation.surface: A medical examination for a doctor working on an assembly line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Test' is a cricket or rugby Test match, played between nations.
explanation.definitionFit: A Test match is played between national sides, so it is an international fixture.

clue.text: Oration delivered in Canada

indicators.note: a speech delivered is spoken out, here read as the speech's letters set free and rearranged

explanation.surface: A speech given somewhere in Canada.
explanation.definitionFit: Ontario is one of Canada's provinces, home to Toronto and Ottawa, so it lies in that country.

clue.text: Drink for sergeant at northern French city

parts.note: ale is a drink
a sergeant is a non-commissioned officer, NCO

explanation.surface: A drink bought for a soldier in a northern French town.
explanation.definitionFit: Alencon is a city in Normandy, known for its lace.

clue.text: Fine for old and young alike

definitions.meaning: old-fashioned slang for fine or excellent
a British comic read by children and adults

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition describes the Dandy, the long-running British comic that is the puzzle's theme.
explanation.definitionFit: Dandy is informal for splendid, and the Dandy comic entertained readers of every age.

clue.text: Hopeless part of 12 in 12: will telepathy find monarch in time?

indicators.note: the telepathy and the monarch are placed inside the word for time

parts.note: a date is a point in time
ESP, extrasensory perception, includes telepathy
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen

explanation.surface: Will a mind-reader locate the sovereign before it is too late?
explanation.walkthrough: 'part of 12 in 12' adds that the word is half of Desperate Dan, a character in the Dandy.
explanation.definitionFit: Desperate can describe a situation so dire it is beyond hope.

clue.text: Change of leader for 'orse?

indicators.note: the dropped aitch in this spelling of horse shows the H is to be lost

parts.note: a halter is the rope by which a horse is led

explanation.surface: A question about swapping the lead rope for a Cockney's horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'orse is horse said without its H, so the halter is said the same way.
explanation.definitionFit: To alter something is to change it, a direct verb synonym.

clue.text: Copy concerned with backing Mussolini

parts.note: re means concerning or about
pro means in favour of, supporting
Il Duce was Mussolini's title

explanation.surface: Someone involved with supporting the Italian dictator.
explanation.definitionFit: To reproduce something is to make a copy of it.

clue.text: Don't allow an article on island character in 12

parts.note: to ban is to not allow
a is the indefinite article
the Isle of Man

explanation.surface: Banning a newspaper piece about an island figure in the comic.
explanation.walkthrough: Bananaman was a superhero strip in the Dandy (originally in Nutty).
explanation.definitionFit: Bananaman is a comic-strip superhero whose adventures ran in the Dandy.

clue.text: Two pound return on gold at church, used by 13 character as razor

indicators.note: the two pieces before it are read backwards together

parts.note: taken as the word two
lb is the abbreviation for a pound weight
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: A two-pound bet returns on gold at church, used by a comic character to shave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return' turns TWOLB into BLOWT. Desperate Dan, the Dandy's strongman, shaves his bristly chin with a blowtorch.
explanation.definitionFit: In the comic strip Desperate Dan's stubble is so tough that he shaves it off with a blowtorch flame.

clue.text: Mouth with no heart, evidence of camphor having been applied?

indicators.note: the central letter of the word mouth is removed

parts.note: proof is evidence

explanation.surface: Someone sniffs at a mouth smelling of camphor, asking whether it has been used.
explanation.walkthrough: Camphor was a traditional moth repellent, so clothes treated with it are protected.
explanation.definitionFit: Camphor deters clothes moths, so items treated with it are protected against them.

clue.text: Figure of speakers entering, not well oiled

indicators.note: the speakers go into the jumbled word
something not well is out of order, signalling a rearrangement

parts.note: lips form speech, so they are speakers

explanation.surface: A figure of speech from talkers arriving, not properly lubricated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Figure of speakers' poses as 'figure of speech'; 'Figure' alone is the definition, a geometric solid. 'not well' makes ELOID from the oiled letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An ellipsoid is a geometric figure, a solid whose cross-sections are ellipses.

clue.text: Group and so on going into reverse

indicators.note: the whole construction is turned round to read backwards
the words for and so on go inside the next word

parts.note: into means to, as in going into town

explanation.surface: A band of musicians, and others, slipping into reverse gear.
explanation.walkthrough: Araucaria reads 'into' both ways: it is the container signal and also supplies TO, giving TETCO before 'reverse' turns it to read the other way.
explanation.definitionFit: An octet is a group of eight, especially eight musicians playing together.

clue.text: One making selfish use of would-be liberators imprisoned by one going out, perhaps

indicators.note: the liberators are held inside the one leaving

parts.note: an exiter is someone who exits
the PLO, Palestine Liberation Organization

explanation.surface: Freedom fighters jailed by a departing ruler are being used.
explanation.definitionFit: An exploiter takes unfair advantage, using others selfishly.

clue.text: God, lawyer and beast going by car?

parts.note: Pan is the Greek god of the wild
a DA is a district attorney

explanation.surface: A deity, an attorney and an animal take a drive.
explanation.walkthrough: A panda car was a British police patrol car, named for its black-and-white livery.
explanation.definitionFit: The panda is a bear, and a panda car was the British police patrol vehicle.

clue.text: Swift and quiet in attack

indicators.note: the quiet letter goes inside the attack

parts.note: a raid is an attack
P, piano, is the musical direction for quiet

explanation.surface: A fast and silent assault.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapid means fast or quick, a plain synonym.

clue.text: 12 23 down's fruit to order

definitions.note: the surname of the Dandy's Harry

parts.note: a hip is the fruit of the rose
PO is a postal order

explanation.surface: A comic character's fruit is made to order.
explanation.walkthrough: Harry Hippo was a character in the Dandy comic.
explanation.definitionFit: Harry Hippo was a Dandy strip, so this completes the name of that character.

clue.text: Vex 12 character

definitions.meaning: ... Hippo was a Dandy strip character

explanation.definitionFit: To harry is to keep annoying someone, and Harry was the first name of a Dandy hippo.

clue.text: Lethargy does for love in a primate

indicators.note: the letter for love goes inside the primate

parts.note: a langur is an Asian monkey
O is love, the zero score in tennis

explanation.surface: Sluggishness serves as affection inside a monkey.
explanation.definitionFit: Languor is a pleasant tiredness or listlessness, close to lethargy.

clue.text: Garden feature backed by a record agent

indicators.note: the run of pieces after it is read backwards

parts.note: a log is a record
a rep is a sales representative, an agent

explanation.surface: A garden structure endorsed by a recording agent.
explanation.definitionFit: A pergola is an arbour of posts and beams over a garden walk, supporting climbing plants.

clue.text: Tokay, heated mistakenly, following pages? Don't go to work!

indicators.note: letters put in by mistake are wrongly placed, so they are rearranged

parts.note: ff is the abbreviation for and the following pages

explanation.surface: Warming a sweet Hungarian wine by mistake, then reading on: why not skip the office?
explanation.walkthrough: Tokay is a sweet Hungarian dessert wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking the day off means not going to work for that day, an idiom given here as an imperative.
